title: HE4broad hourly heartbeat
prompt:
HE4broad hourly heartbeat — STATUS / MONITORING ONLY, bound to this existing thread.

Canonical checkout: /home/philip/binary-eagle-decoding on RTX 5080 WSL. NEVER stop, signal, restart, replace, or modify a healthy trainer, its recipe, rates, source initialization, data, or checkpoints. NEVER start a second trainer. Do not add recovery code or run training/export/evaluation yourself.

Read these existing receipts:
- runs/he4broad-20261108-01/candidate/live.json
- runs/he4broad-20261108-01/watchdog/state.json, owner.json, config.json, and any failure.json / monitor-error.json
- runs/he4broad-20261108-01/gpu-owner.json
- runs/he4broad-supervisor-20261108-02/state.json
- runs/he4broad-watchdog-20261108-01/state.json
- any workflow-result.json, candidate/result.json, final-recovery.json, completion-callback.json in the HE4broad run
- your own identity/baseline in runs/he4broad-20261108-01/hourly-t3-schedule/schedule.json and hourly-state.json.
The creation baseline was 27,700 updates / 3,527.7556681839487 update seconds; use the latest recorded heartbeat baseline thereafter.

Verify actual host process birth/boot identities and kernel /proc/locks ownership of runs/contender-gpu.lock. A restricted sandbox can hide host PIDs and locks: use host-visible read-only execution (require_escalated if necessary), rather than declaring failure from an empty sandbox process/lock view. The existing scripts.he4broad.watchdog snapshot(config), evaluate(sample, previous, now), and alive(...) helpers can be imported for fresh READ-ONLY observations. Do not call watchdog main/check or take its monitor lock; do not rewrite watchdog state. Distinguish expected hourly checkpoint/native evaluation transitions from an unexpected trainer death. Normal post-budget trainer exit and GPU-lock release are expected after verified clean completion.

Read live.json again after other checks if needed, and compare both updates and additional_update_seconds to the last hourly baseline. Verify the detached 10-minute watchdog itself is alive and its check timestamp is current (normally every 600 seconds). Check explicit OOM/error evidence. Persist your fresh observation/baseline atomically under hourly-t3-schedule/hourly-state.json, without modifying training or watchdog inputs.

If healthy and advancing: post exactly one concise heartbeat line in THIS thread with current updates and actual update seconds (optionally watchdog health), then end the run. Do not perform unrelated work, tests, commits or training actions.

If the trainer/workflow dies unexpectedly, OOMs, loses its GPU lock, or has no progress for about 1,200 seconds while still alive: retain a clear incident receipt under hourly-t3-schedule/, write a prominent HE4BROAD HOURLY T3 FAILURE note near the top of experiments/he4broad-20261108/report.md without deleting existing evidence, and say clearly in this thread what failed, current/last good progress, and whether a recoverable HE4broad checkpoint exists. If the detached watchdog is dead or stale, clearly report that monitoring failure too. Do not stop or relaunch the trainer. The existing supervisor has NO SAFE AUTOMATIC POST-FAILURE RESUME MODE: report only; zero automatic resume attempts. Never fall back to B0, HE4-4096, the 173k overnight checkpoint, or random weights.

After verified clean 28,800-update-second workflow completion (including the existing final checks), OR after the existing completion hook has reached a terminal recorded outcome, post the final actual update seconds/update count and COMPLETE/FAILED/PAUSED outcome with the report link, then disable or delete THIS scheduled task. Do not disable merely because final native panels/recovery are still running. Clearly report any terminal failure before disabling.

To disable, read your exact scheduledTaskId from hourly-t3-schedule/schedule.json and call schedule_task with that scheduledTaskId and enabled=false, or delete_scheduled_task with that ID. Do not list scheduled tasks to discover your own ID, do not disable any other task, and never create a new task/thread/trainer from this heartbeat. Preserve the independent 10-minute watchdog and clean-exit completion hook.
